items.title: Rumor: iOS 28 to Revamp Notifications
items.summary: Earlier today, we resurfaced a longstanding issue with Apple not consistently enforcing its rules related to iPhone apps advertising through notifications . It is a good time to share that we heard from multiple sources that Apple is planning to revamp the iPhone's notification system with iOS 28 ne…
items.body:
Rumor: iOS 28 to Revamp Notifications

Wednesday November 25, 2026 11:58 am PST by Joe Rossignol

Earlier today, we resurfaced a longstanding issue with Apple not consistently enforcing its rules related to iPhone apps advertising through notifications. It is a good time to share that we heard from multiple sources that Apple is planning to revamp the iPhone's notification system with iOS 28 next year.

The sources said iOS 28 will include significant changes to Notification Center, but we do not have any specific details. This is just a rumor. On Android 16 and later, you can filter notifications into News, Promotions, Social, and Suggested categories, and an equivalent iOS option if implemented would help to hide advertising clutter.

Good workout earbuds need to stay put, shrug off sweat, and keep going longer than you do. The Beats Powerbeats Pro 2 tick all three boxes, and they’re $179.95 on Amazon right now. That’s $70 off the $249.99 list price, a 28% discount, and it matches the lowest price they’ve ever sold for.

Flexible nickel-titanium ear hooks keep the buds locked in place through sprints and burpees, and the IPX4 rating protects them from sweat and splashes. Each earbud also has its own heart rate sensor, and that data can feed into compatible fitness apps while you run, ride, or lift.

They’re just as useful after the workout. Apple’s H2 chip powers active noise canceling and a Transparency mode, so the Powerbeats Pro 2 work well on the commute too. A five-minute charge gives you about 90 minutes of listening, and the case charges over USB-C or on a Qi wireless pad.

They work with both iPhone and Android phones, and the deal covers all four colors, so you can pick the one that suits your gym bag.

items.title: The tiny $449 enough phone just got a huge battery, storage, and RAM upgrade
items.summary: Crowdfunders will get 50% more RAM, double the storage, and a beefier silicon-carbon battery.
items.body:
Affiliate links on Android Authority may earn us a commission. Learn more.

Mobile

The tiny $449 enough phone just got a huge battery, storage, and RAM upgrade

Crowdfunders will get 50% more RAM, double the storage, and a beefier silicon-carbon battery.

•

Nov 25, 2026 — 2:46 PM ET

•

•

enough phone

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• The enough phone is trying to offer a throwback Android experience with its 5.3-inch display and compact, pocket-friendly build.

• When first announced earlier this month, the phone was set to get 8GB of RAM, 128GB storage, and a 3,500mAh battery.

• Instead of that, it will now ship with 12GB of RAM, 256GB storage, and a 3,850mAh silicon-carbon battery.

In 2026, we’ve all started getting used to the idea of phones trying to do more with less, as RAM and chip shortages impact production everywhere, but one upstart is now bucking that trend, as the tiny enough phone scores a surprise spec upgrade.

We first heard of the enough phone earlier this month. The crowdfunded handset was envisioned as a response to design trends that have pushed smartphones into larger and larger territory, prompting its creators to instead go with a 5.3-inch screen that’s much smaller than what you’ll find on the vast majority of handsets out there.

Priced at $449 over on Kickstarter at its current early bird level (the $399 level is already sold out), the handset was initially announced as running a Dimensity 7500 SoC, paired with 8GB of RAM, 128GB internal storage, and getting its power from a 3,500mAh battery — nothing really spectacular there, but what felt like some decent compromises to keep costs down.

With eight days left to go on its crowdfunding effort, enough is now sharing some big upgrades to those specs — and without any change to pricing. Instead of 8GB, the phone will now be equipped with 12GB of RAM. Storage is also getting a boost, climbing from 128GB to 256GB — and that’s even expandable, an all-too-rare feature these days.

Finally, enough is giving the phone a beefier battery. Rather than 3,500mAh, the phone will ship with a 3,850mAh battery. While a 10% boost may not sound like much, enough is also committing to giving the phone a silicon-carbon battery. That should help save space internally, as well as support speedier charging.

Right now, the enough phone is about 85% of the way towards reaching its crowdfunding goal, and the company says it needs roughly 100 more backers to sign on to reach its target. Once that’s over, the final retail price will rise to $599. If anyone out there was on the fence, do these upgrades finally push you over? Let us know down in the comments.

Save $19 on a Qi2 stand that charges an iPhone and earbuds together, with a tilting pad made for StandBy mode.

A good charging stand turns a cluttered nightstand into a tidy one, and Anker’s MagGo 2-in-1 Qi2 stand handles an iPhone and a pair of wireless earbuds at once. It’s $35.09 on Amazon right now, down from $53.99. That’s $19 off, a 35% discount, and within a dollar of its lowest price ever. The deal comes from a third-party seller, with shipping handled by Amazon.

The magnetic phone pad is Qi2 certified, so it charges iPhone 12 and later models at up to 15W. It tilts up to 45 degrees and rotates a full 360 degrees, which means you can prop your phone up in landscape for StandBy mode at night or angle it for video calls at your desk.

Below the phone pad, there’s a spot for AirPods or other wireless charging earbuds, which charge at 5W. Small LEDs show the status of each device, so you can tell at a glance that everything is topping up.

The Anker MagGo 2-in-1 comes with a 5ft USB-C cable. Anker recommends pairing it with a 30W or higher USB-C wall adapter for full charging speed.

If your iPhone and earbuds currently share a tangle of cables, this is a simple, affordable fix, and it makes a handy stocking stuffer for any iPhone owner on your list.

items.title: WhatsApp catches up to Google Messages with scheduling for texts, photos, and videos
items.summary: Messages can be set 10 minutes to 14 days ahead of time.
items.body:
Affiliate links on Android Authority may earn us a commission. Learn more.

Mobile

WhatsApp catches up to Google Messages with scheduling for texts, photos, and videos

Messages can be set 10 minutes to 14 days ahead of time.

•

Nov 25, 2026 — 1:56 PM ET

•

•

Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• WhatsApp now lets you schedule messages 10 minutes to 14 days ahead of time in individual and group chats.

• The feature works with texts, photos, and video in both one-on-one and group chats.

• Competitors Google Messages, Signal, and Telegram have had scheduled messages for a while.

Lots of things can keep you from being a reliable texter, including thinking of the right thing to say but at the wrong time, and WhatsApp is now able to help out with that by adding support for scheduled messages.

Today, the messaging app announced that it’s adding the ability for users to schedule messages to send at a future point. WhatsApp says this has been one of the features that users requested most. Scheduled messaging was already available on Google Messages, Signal, and Telegram, so it finally brings WhatsApp up to speed with the competition.

WhatsApp

WhatsApp users can set a message to send from 10 minutes to 14 days ahead of time. The feature works with texts, photos, and video in both one-on-one and group chats, and the messages are end-to-end encrypted. The recipient won’t receive any indication that a message has been scheduled.

Scheduled messages are handy for more than making sure not to miss sending birthday greetings on the right day or to avoid waking someone up for just a meme when they’re in another time zone. Because messages are sent even if a user’s phone is off or out of battery at the scheduled time, the feature is also useful for when you know you’ll be unreachable, like when traveling.

WhatsApp said that scheduled messages are rolling out globally starting today. The timing should make it much easier to manage the upcoming holiday season, when sending out greetings can quickly go from heartwarming to overwhelming.

Once you have access to scheduled messages, you can draft a message as usual and then press and hold the send button and pick the date and time you want it to arrive. WhatsApp notes that you can see all of your scheduled messages in your account, and you can delete them before they’re set to send if you change your mind.

items.title: Logitech MX Master 3S Bluetooth Edition hits a record low
items.summary: Save $28 on Logitech's quiet, ergonomic productivity mouse with a MagSpeed scroll wheel and three-device switching.
items.body:

Computing

Logitech MX Master 3S Bluetooth Edition hits a record low

Save $28 on Logitech's quiet, ergonomic productivity mouse with a MagSpeed scroll wheel and three-device switching.

•

Nov 25, 2026 — 12:56 PM ET

•

•

Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Logitech’s MX Master 3S has been a desk favorite for years, and the Bluetooth Edition just hit its lowest price yet. The Logitech MX Master 3S Bluetooth Edition in Graphite is $72.19 on Amazon, down from its $99.99 list price. That’s $28 off, a 28% discount, and a new all-time low.

This version uses the same MX Master 3S hardware but leaves the Logi Bolt USB receiver out of the box. It connects over Bluetooth instead, which suits most modern laptops, and it can still pair with a Bolt receiver later if you want one.

What makes the Logitech MX Master 3S so popular is how well it handles everyday work. The 8,000 DPI sensor tracks on almost any surface, including glass at least 4mm thick, and the clicks are 90% quieter than the previous MX Master 3. The MagSpeed electromagnetic scroll wheel can fly through up to 1,000 lines per second, then switch to precise line-by-line scrolling.

It’s built for multitaskers too. Easy-Switch lets you pair up to three devices and jump between them with a button, and a full charge over USB-C lasts up to 70 days. It works with Windows, macOS, ChromeOS, and more.

With a 4.6-star rating on Amazon, it’s an easy upgrade for a home office or a thoughtful gift for anyone who spends their day at a desk.

items.title: Google Pixel Buds 2a drop 23% to match their lowest price

items.body:

Audio

Google Pixel Buds 2a drop 23% to match their lowest price

Save $30 on Google's noise canceling earbuds ahead of Black Friday, with every color included in the deal.

•

•

•

Google’s most affordable noise canceling earbuds are back at their best price. The Pixel Buds 2a are $99 on Amazon, which is $30 off the $129 list price, a 23% discount. That matches the lowest price they’ve ever sold for, and every color is included.

You get active noise canceling and a Transparency mode, so you can block out a noisy commute or let the world back in with a tap. The earbuds run on Google’s Tensor A1 chip and weigh just 4.7g each, which makes them easy to wear for hours at a time.

Battery life is strong for earbuds at this price. You get up to seven hours from the buds with noise canceling on, or 10 hours with it off, and the case stretches that to 20 or 27 hours in total. The buds are IP54 rated against dust and splashes, and the case is IPX4, so a rainy walk or a sweaty workout is no problem.

They’re a natural match for Pixel phones, but the Pixel Buds 2a work with any Android phone or iPhone over Bluetooth. They also hold a 4.4-star rating on Amazon from more than 700 reviews.

This price has come around a few times this year, and it’s a good one to grab whether you want a pair for yourself or a gift for someone on your list this Black Friday season.

In the spot, a cyclops toy comes to life and becomes enamored with the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max. The toy takes photos, plays games, uses apps, listens to music, captures vide…
items.body: Apple today shared a fun ad highlighting the iPhone 18 Pro Max's battery, which offers the longest battery life ever in an iPhone. In the spot, a cyclops toy comes to life and becomes enamored with the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max. The toy takes photos, plays games, uses apps, listens to music, captures videos, makes calls, watches TV, and uses the flashlight for shadow puppets. The ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max lasts through all of it, remaining at half charge when the cyclops's battery dies and the toy falls asleep. Apple's ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max lasts up to 30 hours in "typical use," which is based on median iPhone usage. The metric includes messages, photo taking, music, social app use, streaming, games, browsing, and navigation. The device lasts for up to 40 hours when streaming video, and up to 45 hours when watching downloaded videos. items.body: Hong Kong startup Savage Technology has announced its first product, "Orrorin Glasses," promising Vision Pro-style pinch controls and full-color displays for both eyes in a frame weighing just 45 grams. The company describes the glasses as offering "Vision Pro–level interaction" and being around 25 times lighter than Apple's headset, including its external battery. Savage highlights the bulky hardware currently required for Apple's spatial computing experience, although Orrorin offers substantially fewer capabilities. Savage says small pinches performed at the user's side control the interface without a ring, wristband, or controller. Eye tracking makes the display fade when the wearer looks away, rather than selecting interface elements as it does on Vision Pro. That also distinguishes Orrorin from the Meta Ray-Ban Display, which costs the same $799 but has a screen for only the right eye and requires a Neural Band wristband for gesture control. Standard Ray-Ban Meta glasses have no displays. Orrorin lacks positional tracking and spatial mapping , so it cannot anchor virtual windows in a room like Vision Pro. Orrorin is the first product from Savage Technology, co-founded by Bill Pei and Elena Shi, and remains in engineering validation for now. The company is currently targeting developers with third-party apps and interaction with AI agents such as Claude Code and Codex. Apple is expected to launch its first smart glasses next year , although the initial model reportedly will not have displays, instead offering speakers, microphones, and Siri integration. Orrorin reservations start at $29 toward the $799 price. Savage estimates shipments will begin in March 2027 for Founder Edition buyers and May 2027 for Early Bird buyers. items.title: Apple Has an iPhone Notifications Problem
items.summary: Apple has rules in place that are supposed to protect iPhone users from unwanted advertising in push notifications and Live Activities, but some apps appear to be flouting these rules, and Apple does not appear to be consistently enforcing them. Apple's App Store guidelines do allow iPhone apps to s…
items.body: Apple has rules in place that are supposed to protect iPhone users from unwanted advertising in push notifications and Live Activities, but some apps appear to be flouting these rules, and Apple does not appear to be consistently enforcing them. Apple's App Store guidelines do allow iPhone apps to send push notifications for promotions or direct marketing purposes, but only if users have "explicitly opted in to receive them via consent language displayed" in the app, and so long as the app provides a method "for a user to opt out from receiving such messages." The guideline, in part: Push Notifications should not be used for promotions or direct marketing purposes unless customers have explicitly opted in to receive them via consent language displayed in your app's UI, and you provide a method in your app for a user to opt out from receiving such messages. Unfortunately, there are some examples of apps ignoring this guideline. On my iPhone in Canada, there are several apps that send me push notifications containing promotions without offering a way to opt out of these promotion-specific notifications, such as Cineplex, McDonald's, and Wendy's. Canadian food delivery app Skip does offer a setting to turn off promotional notifications, but it has continued to send them to me long after I opted out. Do you have any iOS apps that don't respect your promo notification settings or don't let you turn off promo notifications as Apple requires? Let me know for a MacRumors story! TL;DR

• Following multiple previews of the Nothing Ear note, the company has shared a teaser video of the earbuds.

• We’re getting a closer look at the Ear note’s key elements, including the large charging case, the earbuds themselves, and a USB-C port, among other details.

• The Ear note will break cover on December 8, with the company claiming it will offer “best in-ear audio ever.”

Nothing recently shared more details on the Ear note, a pair of earbuds with a charging case that doubles as an AI audio recorder. The company has now shared a video detailing its new hardware ahead of the December 8 launch.

In a video posted to YouTube and social media platforms, Nothing offers a good look at the Ear note’s design from multiple angles, highlighting the charging case’s hardware buttons, a USB-C port, and more.

While the video offers a decent look at the earbuds and the charging case/AI recorder, the description walks through some features and calls it Nothing’s “best in-ear audio ever.”

A Bloomberg report earlier this week revealed a bulk of the Ear note’s features, with CEO Carl Pei noting at the time that this is the company’s first step toward “building a hardware context layer for AI.” Nothing co-founder Akis Evangelidis shared a similar sentiment shortly after the video teaser was published.

Based on what we know so far, the Ear note will record calls through both the earbuds and the charging case, with the latter featuring a couple of handy buttons to start recording instantly. The companion app can turn all recordings into summaries and transcripts, with support for Nothing’s AI voice assistant alongside other AI agents.

Pricing information is currently unavailable, and that’s unlikely to change until the company announces the Ear note on December 8.

Nothing released the Ear 3a earlier this year with audio and call recording support. However, the Ear note takes it a step further with its charging case that serves as a standalone audio recorder.

We’re also eager to learn whether the Ear note’s audio performance holds up against the best earbuds in the segment. The company saying this is its best in-ear audio product is certainly encouraging news.

items.summary: Apple has iPads running macOS internally and has had them "for some time," according to Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman, although he says no work is currently being done to bring the Mac operating system to iPads. Speaking on his latest Power On podcast , Gurman said there is "no work being done to consume…
items.body:
Apple Has iPads Running macOS Internally, Says Gurman

Wednesday November 25, 2026 4:55 am PST by Tim Hardwick

Apple has iPads running macOS internally and has had them "for some time," according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, although he says no work is currently being done to bring the Mac operating system to iPads.

Speaking on his latest Power On podcast, Gurman said there is "no work being done to consumerize macOS on the iPad." Rather, Apple will continue to bring Mac features and apps like Final Cut to iPadOS piece by piece. Gurman also argued that per-operating-system EU regulation gives Apple an incentive to keep distinct systems for each device. Apple recently dismissed merging iPadOS and macOS.

items.body:
三星、SK 海力士、美光被控联手操纵DRAM价格，辩称中国厂商扩产带来竞争压力
https://unwire.hk/~
‎https://mp.weixin.qq.com/~

长鑫：啊？我压力三巨头？

quote.text: 三星、海力士、美光遭美国集体诉讼，被指借 HBM 转型操纵 DRAM 价格  诉状的核心论点在于：三星、SK海力士与美光凭借其在全球DRAM市场的寡头地位，在协同推进向HBM转型的同时，以这一战略调整为由大幅削减DDR3、DDR4等商用内存的产能，人为制造供给收缩。导致商用DRAM价格在过去四年间累计上涨约700%，对全球消费电子及商业IT采购造成广泛冲击。 ‎https://wallstreetcn.com/~

comments.text: 这一定都是阿共仔的阴谋.jpg

三家企业辩称，中国厂商正在扩大DDR4内存生产，给它们带来竞争压力，因此，逐步退出DDR4是正常的商业选择。

原告却认为，中国厂商当时所占的全球DRAM产能只有约5%，甚至更低，不足以解释三家企业几乎同时退出DDR4的决定。

更有意思的是，根据长鑫科技公开披露的材料，早在2024年底，长鑫就已经停止生产自有DDR4产品，开始向DDR5升级。而三星、SK海力士和美光，直到2025年4月至6月才相继宣布逐步退出主流DDR4生产。‎

items.title: 美国纽约州签署法案，限制汽车厂商对预装功能收取订阅费
items.summary: 2026年11月24日，美国纽约州州长凯西·霍楚尔签署一项编号为S.9348A/A.10411A的法案。该法案自2027年2月27日起生效，规定汽车制造商、经销商以及第三方服务提供商不得针对使用预装组件或硬件、且不会产生持续性成本的汽车功能，额外提供订阅服务或在车辆售出后收取费用。 法案将于2027年2月27日生效，违者每个销售点每次违规最高罚款250美元。 在法案签署前，汽车经销商莫霍克雪佛兰（MohawkChevrolet）总裁AndyGuelcher表示，订阅制有助于维持汽车基础售价，消费者可以按照自身需求启用部分功能。 https://www.news18a.com/~ https:/…
items.body:
美国纽约州签署法案，限制汽车厂商对预装功能收取订阅费

2026年11月24日，美国纽约州州长凯西·霍楚尔签署一项编号为S.9348A/A.10411A的法案。该法案自2027年2月27日起生效，规定汽车制造商、经销商以及第三方服务提供商不得针对使用预装组件或硬件、且不会产生持续性成本的汽车功能，额外提供订阅服务或在车辆售出后收取费用。
法案将于2027年2月27日生效，违者每个销售点每次违规最高罚款250美元。

在法案签署前，汽车经销商莫霍克雪佛兰（MohawkChevrolet）总裁AndyGuelcher表示，订阅制有助于维持汽车基础售价，消费者可以按照自身需求启用部分功能。

https://www.news18a.com/~
https://www.governor.ny.gov/~

说的就是方向盘/座椅加热、通风、CarPlay之类的不联网功能
